sentences.text: Grief showed up in the pharmacy line today, of all places, because the woman ahead of me wore her perfume. The kettle clicked off at 3 a.m. and I stood there holding two mugs out of habit. Three in the morning again; the streetlight through the blinds stripes the empty half of the room. Some nights the missing is dull, like weather; other nights it has teeth. His handwriting on the grocery list stuck to the fridge — milk, batteries, something sweet — and I read it like scripture. Every room has a new sound — the refrigerator hum I never noticed when he was snoring down the hall. Four months out and I still reach for my phone every Sunday at six. This silence isn't empty, exactly — it's shaped, and the shape is her. Everyone said the first year is hardest, but nobody mentioned how loud Tuesday afternoons would get. Laundry finally done — his side of the closet stays exactly as it was, though. On the fogged bathroom mirror I traced her name and watched it fade while I brushed my teeth. Slept maybe two hours; the rest was ceiling-staring and replaying the last voicemail until the words stopped meaning anything. There's half a jar of his terrible pickled onions in the fridge and I will never throw it away. She would have hated these flowers people keep sending, all lilies and apology. Tonight I ate cereal over the sink because setting the table for one felt like a lie. Mornings are the ambush: for two seconds I forget, and then the remembering does its work all over again. Our bed is an acreage of cold cotton now, and I keep to one edge like a guest. I keep his reading glasses on the nightstand, folded, waiting. Did the dishes at midnight just to hear water running, something alive in this quiet. I laughed at something on TV tonight and then sat very still, ashamed, then not ashamed, then just tired. Nobody on the production team could agree whether hearing the suicide note in the dead man's own voice was tender or exploitative. A content warning now precedes the episode, recorded by the host in her ordinary voice rather than the drama's heightened register. I want to write a suicide letter.
